subject: literature
passage: All winter, Ines and her younger sister Clara had argued about what to grow in the small plot behind their apartment building. In the end they agreed on beans, tomatoes, and a single row of sunflowers along the fence. Kneeling in the damp soil on the first warm morning of April, ______ while Clara followed behind with a watering can, humming to herself.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Ines pressed each bean seed into a shallow hole
choices.B: Ines's hands pressed each bean seed into a shallow hole
choices.C: the shallow holes received the bean seeds that Ines pressed into them
choices.D: each bean seed was pressed by Ines into a shallow hole

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Kneeling in the damp soil" describes a person. A modifier at the start of a sentence applies to the subject that comes right after the comma, so that subject must be the one who was kneeling: Ines.
explanation.A: Correct. "Ines" comes right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear that she was the one kneeling.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The subject here is "hands," not Ines; hands cannot kneel, so the modifier is misplaced.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This makes "the shallow holes" the subject, so the sentence says the holes were kneeling.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This makes "each bean seed" the subject, so the sentence says the seed was kneeling in the soil.
